Love & Lace - The Grinch that Stole my Wedding

By: Mosibudi Ratlebjane | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
She is a slippery scamster and repeat offender, Yolanda van Vuren has no shame in her game. For years Love and Lace has been her cash cow, with countless victims seeking justice against her and her fa

Unique Selling Point:
Lindie aka Yolanda van Vuren can be best described as the Grinch of all Fairy tale weddings - spending years rucksacking the online streets of social media (e.i facebook) lurring unsuspecting brides and grooms to be, with reasonably priced wedding dresses, suits and all bridalwear. Only to ruin their special day by delivering less than desirable orders - if any at all, and running off and hiding with all their money.

Summary:
Love and Lace, has been in business since 2013, has been the reason for countless bridal tears ever since its inception. Advertising on Facebook, Yolanda has been the subject of a Carte Blanche investigation before, slipping through CB fingers and torturing more victims.

With about 30 odd victims from both bridal boutique and Reborn baby doll business. Yolanda has threatened her customers with legal action after they request their goods and or their money back. She has initiated a voluntary liquidation for her company and threatened her victims with cease and desist letters. She is suspected to be using her brother posing to be a lawyer, and her Pastor father in-law to guilt trip customers when they request their money back.
She knows the law and is cunning in how she does business, making it nearly impossible to open fraud cases against.


Further information:
First Issue:
A number of Love and Lace Victims attempted to open cases against Lindie and were told not that the cases were civil cases, and not criminal. This is where we see how smart Lindie is. By using the criminal justice system to her favour.

Countless of complaints were made on Facebook and other online plaforfms: we speak to an expert on why social media platforms are able to use algorithms to spot, human trafficking, hate speech and other seious crimes but are no able to pick up, negative feedback and warn or even deactivate businesses that are noted to being faulty.

“Scammers are taking advantage of Facebook's advertising options to promote anything they can,” says Molly Borman Heymont, a direct-to-consumer retail entrepreneur. “Facebook does not appear to validate the legitimacy of their advertisers' website or products, so it's more of a buyer beware situation.”


The Confrontation:
Because we know Lindie is a slippery character who is totally aware that there are people contanstanly looking for her. We will stake outside her house, looking at all her movements from two days straight with Philasande and myself. I will also walk around and ask for a domestic worker job, just so as to see if she is in the house.

Her husband has taken over her bridal boutique shop in Veeringering, and has his own business in the building. On a specified shoot day with a presenter we will then confront the husband with Two of the case Studies, demanding to get answers.

Press Release:


Wedding Day Blues

The wedding dress is everything when it comes to most brides’ special day. Many spend months looking for the perfect attire – especially when planning a wedding on a tight budget. Sold on affordable prices for wedding clothes and happy testimonials, some furious brides are crying foul after one bridal boutique took their money but left them with little more than tears and frustration. Carte Blanche investigates what recourse might be available to customers when online offers go awry.

Producer: Mosibudi Ratlebjane | Presenter: Claire Mawisa

Watch the trailer

Script:


VOICE:

1 Harp music - Menique” Wedding Video: And B-Roll designer: Day 1 Phila: VOICE: It’s that teary moment during a wedding when the groom sees his bride walking down the aisle in her special dress. However, one online bridal boutique seemed (or was said to) to throw those dreams in the gutter… leaving some brides tearful before their special day.

2 Jean-Marie #clip1: (12:42) It was just everybody's fault. Except for her. Tiaan (17:48): She never ever wanted to meet never. Mandi Gouws: (10:42) She had excuses that she had to go and fetch, um, packages. Chemoné von Clip#167: (06:38) Just, postponing, postponing. Excuses after excuses.

3 LINK CLIP (08895R): YOU'RE NEWLY ENGAGED, AND ARE PLANNING YOUR FAIRY-TALE WEDDING. THE DRESS HAS TO BE THE STAR OF THE SHOW, BUT WHAT HAPPENS WHEN IT’S A DAY BEFORE YOUR WEDDING DAY, AND YOU STILL DON'T HAVE A DRESS.

4 REWORDED + ORDERED VOICE: On and Off since 2016, Carte Blanche received complaints about a Bridal boutique based in Vereeniging.

5 VOICE: Like Ménique LLoyd and her groom, who alleged that they were left stranded with no attire three days before their wedding.

6 Menique LLoyd: (09:32) My husband is very tall.I have a picture of the suit. It actually fits me. Now. Menique LLoyd (10:26). In the end. It was that Wednesday. My dress was still not there. And my wedding was on Saturday.

7 VOICE: There was Linzi Voster, who paid but hadn’t given her measurements or confirmed her order, when she requested her money back.

8 LINZI VOSTER: (07:13) She just told me that I have a no refund policy whereas, you know what you're not out of pocket was no dresses were ordered.

9 VOICE: Then there was Teresa Rossouw, a Love and Lace agent from Kimberly.

10 Theresa Rossouw: (12:50) I believe in my heart that he didn't start out as a scam, but I think it developed into a scam. Theresa Rossouw: (13:15) she absolutely didn't even order anything from the 15,000 rand that I spent.

11 NEW VOICE: VOICE: Love and Lace Vereeniging, is a bridal boutique that used Facebook to market dresses, suits, and all things wedding attire at reasonable prices.

VOICE: In May 2019, Beaming Bride to be Chemoné van Tonder was impressed with Love and Lace’s numerous promotions.

13 Chemoné van Tonder: #166 (01:11). I am a bride on a budget and they did mention that they just opened in the Vaal. Chemoné van Tonder:#166 (01:38) I decided then to go book a fitting and to meet the lady and to look

at all the dresses and see where we can go from there.

14 VOICE: The lady introduced herself as “Lindy” who owned a shop called Love and Lace in Vereeniging from 2013 until early 2020.

15 Chemoné von TondeClip#167: (22:39) The first thing that bugged me, there wasn't a huge selection, like it was said on facebook. Chemoné von TondeClip#167: (22:39) So she said, not to worry, what I could do was find a dress that I like the most, and what she will do is she will alter it into my dream wedding dress.

16 Circled Dresses; and the changes needed to made: VOICE: Measurements were taken to change the bodice and the back of the dress completely. Since the dress was already in the shop, van Tondered hoped it would be ready in a month’s time, but was told it would take six to eight weeks until her first fitting.

17 Chemoné van Tonder#167 (01:47) Straight after we paid the deposit, we booked the first fitting, I counted eight weeks. (02:31) when we got there on Saturday, she wasn't there. Chemoné van Tonder (03:39 I spoke to her and she said to me at the time, Oh, it's a baby brain. (03:47) I Completely forgot because she was pregnant at the time.

18 Chemoné von TondeClip#167: (06:42) there was a time, um, where she said the dress would be ready, but it's stuck in.Chemoné von TondeClip#167: (06:49) Customs. Now I sat and I thought about it. Why is my dress in customs when you're making it?

19 VOICE: Von Tonder says, Lindie whose Full

name is Yolanda Jansen van Vuren, told her that the dresses were made in Dubai, but were then altered by a seamstress in South Africa.

20 Chemoné von Tonde Clip#167: (16:07) I was actually depressed, annoyed, um, wedding planning wasn't fun anymore. Chemoné von Tonde: (10:26) So I went onto Hello Peter and got the surprise of my life because all these brides are going through all these horrific things. stories.Chemoné von Tonder Clip#167: (12:02). And I sent it to her. I was like, listen, what's going on? Am I getting my dress? Is this a scam?

21 VOICE: Jansen Van Vuren answered her in a voicenote and told Van Tonder not to take online reviews to heart.

22 Voice Note: Lindy Jansen Van Vuren: In terms of the hello peter remark. Any Business in South Africa, will have Hello Peter Remarks: Bride and Co has more than 5 000....it does not make them a bad company. Unfortunately people act at the heat of the moment, Even if a situation is settled and resolved, you cannot remove it. You cannot go based on that and you’ll see it's only done in one month. Please just Just relax a little bit, you are only getting married in April. There is time. So just relax. Please just have a little patience as well.

23 REWORDED + ORDERED VOICE: Unlike Menique, Linzi and Teressa, Van Tonder did at least receive a dress seven months later - stuffed in a less than desirable delivery box.

25 ROR JANSEN VV VOICE: After numerous attempts to contact Jansen van Vuren, she responded to all the

allegations in writing, through her attorney….

26 ROR JANSEN VV VOICE: She stated that the delivery boxes were in line with courier requirements, and she denied misrepresenting where the dresses came from, as she did not recall advising clients that the dresses were custom-made. She added that the Love and Lace pages had said the dresses were imported.

27 ROR JANSEN VV VOICE: She claims Ménique had no grounds for a refund and that Ménique was made aware of the risk of ordering close to the wedding.

28 VOICE: So, could this be a series of Misunderstandings? Mandi Gouws, thinks not. After going through postponed fittings and incorrectly-coloured bridesmaid dresses...she began her own investigation.

29 Mandi Gouws #0808LF (15:04) I left in tears because I thought how I've paid all this money I saw all these complaints going years back. Mandi Gouws #081814: (12:35) At that stage I realised, I think there's problems much bigger than just me.

30 ROR JANSEN VV VOICE: But Jansen van Vuren insists that the errors in orders were caused by her assistant and she says some complaints are exaggerated.

31 Claire Mawisa: Had you ever communicated

with other brides, that were also disappointed by Lindi? Mandi Gouws:081814 (12:50) I had so many brides in tears. Mandi Gouws #081814 : (24:55) We've actually tried to block that page. We notified Facebook what's happening and it kept on going, kept on going until she closed it herself. Mandi Gouws #081814: (11:55) And then we got a lawyer, a lawyer letter threatening us that if we continue to put bad things on, on social media, she'll Sue us.

32 VOICE: Social Media Lawyer Verlie Oosthuizen of Shepstone and Wylie says doing business on social media platforms, is like walking on a tightrope.

33 Verlie Oosthuizen: (00:29) There's definitely a huge marketplace on social media, fraudsters and tricksters. And that is something that you have to be aware of when we are participating in buying things on social media. Claire: So in the case of Love and Lace Customers who had grievances against the company, and complained. Were they well within their rights to do so? Verlie Oosthuizen: (05:31). You've got to be very careful when you are naming and sharing on social media. And the unfortunate thing is that it is so so effective. But, If it's not true and it's not in public interest, it is unlawful and you can be sued for defamation.

34 FACEBOOK ROR VOICE: We asked Facebook why the platform hadn’t shut the page down. Backed by their Terms of Service, Facebook responded that Love and lace was not on Facebook Marketplace, meaning they couldn’t enact certain protocols to shut the account down. And decisions to remove pages are complex and take time.”

35 ROR JANSEN VV VOICE: In her response, Jansen van Vuren said she had a right to block and remove defamatory comments that were personal and abusive, and confirmed she had removed the page herself.

36 VOICE: In early 2020, clients received a shock - that Love and Lace had filed for voluntary liquidation - and they would likely never see their dresses or money.

CHANGE: Insert Legitimate LOVE AND LACE: Websites: LINK WHEN SEARCHING LOVE AND LACE BRIDAL BOUTIQUE ONLINE, THERE ARE MANY VERSIONS OF THE LEGITIMATE BRIDAL BUSINESSES, SOME FROM THE UK, US AND EVEN NEW ZEALAND.

37 REWORDED + ORDERED + INSERT VIDEO RECORDING OF L&L WEBSITE SA: VOICE: There are even South African bridal businesses that have nothing to do with JANSEN VAN VUREN’S LOVE and Lace.

38 LINK: SO, WHEN LINDI’S, LOVE AND LACE WAS LOOKING FOR AGENTS MANY SAW THIS AS A GREAT OPPORTUNITY TO MAKE SOME MONEY.

39 VOICE: In 2015 Jean-Marie Wright convinced her mother Mariette, to use some of her pension money to become a Love and Lace Reselling agent in Secunda. However, their entrepreneurial optimism was short-

lived.

40 Jean-Marie: (01:47) We contacted Lindy, she had contracts, everything, brochures, catalogues. It really looked like the real deal. Jean-Marie (06:09) There wasn't initially a cheap dress that you could buy. They started from five, 6,000 and upwards

41 VOICE: They paid a R30 000 deposit, but within two months their reputations were in tatters and no profit was made.

42 Jean-Marie: (15:22) It went from zero to a hundred, within two months, people were just saying, don't use love and Lace Secunda because you are not going to get your dresses and they are going to steal your money. Jean- Jean-Marie: (03:43) The first order we received Jean-Marie: (04:35) Lindy then says, no, that she's having trouble with customs.

43 VOICE: Jansen van Vuren responded that she had no control over customs and that not every order had been delayed.

44 Jean-Marie: (05:06) We needed to pay the cost price to Lindy for the dress that was ordered. And then we also had to refund the client out of our own pockets. So we made a big loss there. And that is basically what happened with every, with every client.

45 VOICE: Jansen Van Vuren’s version is that refunds were provided, or dresses were remade. She alleges that in rare cases where clients provided incorrect measurements, refunds would not necessarily be applicable. She claims that only a couple of the 38 reselling agents complained and she always afforded

adequate support to the agents.

46 VOICE: The Electronic Communications and Transaction Act protects consumers making purchases online, holding suppliers like Jansen Van Vuren liable. It states that a supplier must have a return, exchange or refund policy and if the supplier is unable to deliver, they must refund the client within 30 days.

47 VOICE: Nearly all the Love and Lace customers we spoke to claim they were not afforded these rights.

48 Nandia Steyn: She is a thief, liar, she’s a liar manipulator and she is a liar and a cheat.

49 Madeline Zwart: Lindie kept on making promises, that it will come. I also received a call from the inspector from the police force saying that the bride opened a case against me.

50 Mandi Gouws: #081814: (15:57) I said to Lindy that last time I spoke to Lindie, you're not going to get away with this. I'm sorry. You cannot do business like this. And she said to me, you do what you want. This is not a criminal case. It will be a civil case. So you do what you want to do.

51 VOICE: This is the same lesson Christian Bekker and his wife learned when they purchased a consignment of 65 dresses and paid 188 thousand Rand…not knowing they would never receive a thread of fabric or lace.

52 TIAAN DAY3 Fourth Card: (13:55)

When she heard what type of investment, I wanted to invest into this, this, uh, endeavour of ours. I mean, then she started pushing for deposits. Then the second deposit, she asked me for a second post, because he said, this is a huge order. Claire Mawisa: (17:07)What, at what point do you then decide that you're going to stop? TIAAN DAY3 Fourth Card: (17:24) After my last payment. I said to my wife, no, no, no, no. This is getting ridiculous...

53 VOICE: After two lump sum payments and months of non-delivery Bekker then wanted to cancel his order and get a refund.

54 TIAAN DAY3 Fourth Card:(21:53) I'm fed up with this story. Now I'm going to, I'm cancelling the order, give me my money back. Oh man. She says, that's not in a contract. I said, listen, I do not have a contract with you. There's never a signed contract between me and you.

55 Claire Mawisa: (30:42) So what were the challenges with opening up a case? TIAAN DAY-3 Fourth Card: (31:18) I went to the police. I want to open a fraud case and explain to them. They asked me, explain the case to me every time they said to me, nothing, Nope. We cannot open a fraud case. It's civil, it's civil, everything. TIAAN DAY3 Fourth Card: (31:41)

Every time it was civil.

56 VOICE: In response, Jansen van Vuren admitted the consignment of dresses was a very large order – she says she offered to fulfil the order partially, and said it was Bekker who declined.

57 VOICE: We asked the South African Police Service why a case like Bekker’s is considered civil and not criminal. National Spokesperson Brigadier Vish Naidoo responded that while officers are not allowed to reject a charge, they have the prerogative to assess complaints and if they believe the elements of a crime are not satisfied, they may decline to open a case.

58 VOICE: With two fraud cases pending, Jansen van Vuren maintains that no fraud was ever committed. It was never her intent to hurt or affect anyone. And she claims for every unhappy bride, there were 5 happy ones.

VOICE: Due to the pending criminal proceedings, Jansen van Vuren, through her lawyers, declined our numerous requests for an interview.

59 Christiaan Bekker (23:54) Lindi, She broke my wife. My wife was this designer. She could design the recess like this. She's constantly in pain because of a stomach in a knot, because that's a lot of money.

TEASERS:

● Something old, something borrowed, something blue and something new --- or at least that’s what brides expected from a Gauteng bridal boutique, instead, some

have been left with tears on their special day.

● Sold on affordable prices for wedding attire and happy testimonials – some furious brides are crying foul after one bridal boutique took their money but left them stranded.

● It’s that fairy-tale moment where a bride says Yes to the dress, but some brides had their dreams turned into a nightmare by one Gauteng Bridal Boutique.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Lindie aka Yolanda van Vuren can be best described as the Grinch of all Fairy tale weddings - spending years rucksacking the online streets of social media (e.i facebook) lurring unsuspecting brides and grooms to be, with reasonably priced wedding dresses, suits and all bridalwear. metadata.Summary: Love and Lace, has been in business since 2013, has been the reason for countless bridal tears ever since its inception. Advertising on Facebook, Yolanda has been the subject of a Carte Blanche investigation before, slipping through CB fingers and torturing more victims. With about 30 odd victims from both bridal boutique and Reborn baby doll business. Yolanda has threatened her customers with legal action after they request their goods and or their money back. She has initiated a voluntary liquidation for her company and threatened her victims with cease and desist letters. She is suspected to be using her brother posing to be a lawyer, and her Pastor father in-law to guilt trip customers when they request their money back. She knows the law and is cunning in how she does business, making it nearly impossible to open fraud cases against.
